messages:
Maya R.: Quick PSA — trying to get redwoodctl v0.9.2 working on WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04) and hit a weird failure when installing the .deb we build in CI. `sudo dpkg -i redwoodctl_0.9.2_amd64.deb` exits with `package architecture (amd64) does not match system (arm64)` even though uname -m reports x86_64 inside WSL.

Jin H.: Hmm that sounds like the package metadata is correct but the host reported arch is wrong. Do you have Windows x86 vs ARM confusion? Is your Windows 11 on ARM?

Maya R.: Windows host is x64, WSL distro is the default distro. Repro steps: freshly provisioned WSL, imported from export from another machine, then `dpkg -i` on the CI-built artifact. Found two issues:
1) The .deb we produce has explicit arch in control file but our CI sometimes picks up QEMU/foreign emulation which can set dpkg to longname arch detection.
2) More importantly, redwoodctl's install script writes symlink to `/usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` and WSL had that path mounted from Windows, causing permission errors.

Omar P.: For the permission thing we had success with: `sudo cp redwoodctl /usr/local/bin && sudo chmod 755 /usr/local/bin/redwoodctl` vs relying on the package to create the symlink. But we should probably avoid writing into mountpoints that are not owned by the distro.

Jin H.: Filing two follow-ups: (A) Make our Debian build robust across QEMU/foreign arch checks (build with --host=...) and (B) change installer to prefer /usr/bin or respect DESTDIR. Also add a note in the docs about WSL mount pitfalls.

Maya R.: Also ran into a config/profile oddity: after migrating some teammates from Windows -> WSL we ended with mixed newline endings in `~/.redwood/config.toml` and duplicated `[profile]` entries. `redwoodctl config list-profiles` returned three entries but `redwoodctl login --profile project-x` applied the token to a different section (the first matching name). Repro: create two profile tables with same `name = "project-x"` but different `endpoint` values and run login. Token goes to the first table even if `--profile` intended the second.

Omar P.: That matches a bug I fixed in a local branch where parser used first match index. We should probably treat `name+endpoint` as the unique key or add `id` field for determinism. Also add CLI validation that warns when duplicate names exist.

Jin H.: Quick workaround: `redwoodctl config edit` will open the config in $EDITOR and you can dedupe manually. For CI, set `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG=/tmp/redwood-config` per job so each runner gets a fresh file.

docs-bot: Suggestion: Add section "WSL and Windows users" to redwoodctl install docs covering mount points, symlink issues, and `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG` override.

Maya R.: Another pain point: `redwoodctl dev --local` in our headless CI triggers interactive SSO (opens browser) and the job hangs. We tried `REDWOOD_API_KEY` but our onboarding flow uses SSO-only token exchange. Would love `--no-browser` and a `--token-stdin` option so CI can pipe in a token.

Omar P.: We have `--token` flagged in master but it's not backported or documented. I can backport a `--token-file` flag that reads a token from disk and skips browser flow. Also will add `--no-browser` to be explicit.

Jin H.: On retries: CI concurrency leads to SSO 429s. Current default is 3 retries with exponential backoff (500ms -> 1s -> 2s) but our IdP rate-limits at burst 2/sec. Proposed additions: env var knobs `REDWOODCTL_AUTH_RETRIES`, `REDWOODCTL_AUTH_BACKOFF_MS`, and `REDWOODCTL_MAX_CONCURRENT_AUTH` to gate concurrent login attempts from a host. That should help orchestrators.

Maya R.: Filed issue #2381 with details and a minimal repro (WSL package + dup profiles + headless SSO). Workaround for now: set `REDWOODCTL_CONFIG` per-run, use `--token` from a secrets store, and avoid shared home volumes in WSL.

redwoodctl-bot: New issue created: #2381 "redwoodctl: WSL install edgecases, duplicate profile handling, and headless auth options" by Maya R. https://github.com/redwood/repo/issues/2381

Omar P.: I'll pick up the token-file backport and the config duplicate-name warning. Jin, can you handle the docs patch for WSL and the env var list?

Jin H.: Yup, putting together PRs for both.

Maya R.: Thanks folks, saved me a day. :party_parrot:
